title: Minimum-degree refinement of the Barát–Thomassen conjecture
statement: Let $T$ be a fixed tree with maximum degree $\Delta_T$, and let $|E(T)|$ denote its number of edges. A graph is **$T$-decomposable** if its edges can be partitioned into sets each inducing a copy of $T$. **Minimum-degree refinement of the Barát–Thomassen conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that every graph that is $f(\Delta_T)$-edge-connected, whose number of edges is divisible by $|E(T)|$, and whose minimum degree is at least $f(|E(T)|)$, is $T$-decomposable. This refinement seeks to replace the dependence on a large edge-connectivity bound by separate bounds involving the tree's maximum degree and size. The source presents it as a proposed refinement; no resolution is supplied.
source_name: Julien Bensmail, Ararat Harutyunyan, Tien-Nam Le and Stéphan Thomassé, “Edge-partitioning a graph into paths: beyond the Barát-Thomassen conjecture”, arXiv:1507.08208 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.08208

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2015). “This conjecture was recently verified by the current authors and Merker .”
